tagline: The global leader in the design, development, manufacture and distribution of performance-driven golf products
hero_kpi_rationale: The company derives more than half of its revenue from consumable products (balls, gloves), which are directly tied to rounds played and therefore recurring, creating a unique structural revenue engine in sports.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total sales after discounts and returns.
kpis.description: Net sales reflect demand from passionate golfers and the strength of the Titleist and FootJoy brands.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Operating profit adjusted for non-recurring charges.
kpis.description: Key indicator of operational performance, excluding non-recurring items such as restructuring expenses.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income attributable to Acushnet shows the company's final profitability.

kpis.name: Consumables Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of sales from disposable products such as balls and gloves.
kpis.description: Consumable products (e.g., Titleist Pro V1 balls) generate recurring demand linked to the number of rounds played.
kpis.signal: Structural advantage: balls and gloves are frequently replaced

kpis.name: Rounds Played US YoY
kpis.explanation: Year-over-year change in the number of golf rounds played in the United States.
kpis.description: The United States, the primary market, recorded moderate growth in rounds played in 2025.
kpis.signal: 1% growth in 2025 vs 2024 in the United States

kpis.name: Rounds Played Global YoY
kpis.explanation: Year-over-year change in the number of golf rounds played globally.
kpis.description: Global demand for golf remains stable, with moderate growth of 2% in 2025.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €2.34 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of €0.94 Bn in the latest year

kpis.name: Rounds Played US vs 2019
kpis.explanation: Change in the number of golf rounds played in the United States since 2019.
kpis.description: Golf in the United States has seen a strong post-pandemic recovery, with a cumulative increase of 25% since 2019.
kpis.signal: 25% increase since 2019, indicating a sustained recovery

kpis.name: Rounds Played Global vs 2019
kpis.explanation: Change in the number of golf rounds played globally since 2019.
kpis.description: The global golf market shows a sustained upward trend since 2019, with a cumulative increase of 22%.

risks.title: Dependence of sales on the number of golf rounds played
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned first in the 'Key Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations' section. The language used ('substantially all of our sales', 'directly related to') highlights a strong dependence. It is weighted by the company's industrial nature.

risks.title: Sensitivity to general economic conditions
risks.score_rationale: This risk is the second key factor mentioned, with strong language ('discretionary purchases', 'affected by consumer spending habits and many macroeconomic factors'). It is classified as 'Macro' due to its link to overall economic conditions.

risks.title: Impact of weather conditions on sales
risks.score_rationale: The weather-related risk is clearly detailed, and its impact on playable days and sales is explained. The language ('would reduce', 'decrease the amount spent') indicates notable severity. It is classified as 'Industriel' as it directly affects golf activity.

risks.title: Foreign currency fluctuation risks
risks.score_rationale: Over 40% of sales are generated internationally, exposing the company to foreign exchange risk. The text mentions exposure to 'transaction risk' and 'currency translation risk'. The 'Macro' category is appropriate for this risk.

risks.title: Dependence on new product launch cycles
risks.score_rationale: The document details launch cycles for golf balls and clubs, and notes that announcements of new products may lead to purchase deferrals. This risk relates to innovation and product life cycles, justifying the 'Technology' category.

risks.title: Risks related to the implementation of a new ERP system
risks.score_rationale: The company is in the process of implementing a new global ERP system, with significant costs already incurred and activities planned over several years. Integration and efficiency risks are inherent in such technology projects.

ai_positioning.summary: The company GOLF does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.
